Hi there—I’m so glad you’re here. My name is [Your Name], and I’m a clinician who specializes in the emotional well-being of new mothers. Over the next few minutes I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s a brief, 10-question screen that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling during the past seven days, so we can make sure you’re getting the support you deserve in this postpartum period.

Everything you share stays completely confidential, and this is a judgment-free space—no right or wrong answers, just your honest experience. After each question, feel free to tell me what feels true for you; I’ll keep track of everything privately.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve still been able to laugh sometimes—like when my older son makes silly faces at the baby—but most of the day it feels like I’m just going through the motions. The little giggles don’t last long before I’m back to feeling tired and kind of flat.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… I guess I’d say “sometimes.” I can still laugh here and there—like when my toddler tries to teach the baby how to dance—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to, and the feeling fades pretty fast.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I still look forward to little stuff—like when my mom comes over to help so I can take a shower—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. Mostly I’m just hoping nothing goes wrong.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times. Like, if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I start thinking maybe I’m doing something wrong—maybe I’m not feeding him well enough or I missed some cue. I know it’s probably not fair to myself, but those thoughts still pop in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I’d say “yes, quite a lot.” Even when everything seems fine—baby’s sleeping, no fever, he’s eating okay—I still catch myself checking if he’s breathing or wondering if that little cough means something awful. It’s like my mind keeps circling back to “what if?”
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicked, but a couple of times, out of nowhere, my heart races and I get this tight feeling in my chest—like when I’m rocking the baby at 3 a.m.—and I can’t pin down why. It passes pretty fast, though; I haven’t had a full-blown panic spell.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days it feels like I’m just one tiny thing away from dropping the ball. Yesterday the dishes piled up and the baby wouldn’t nap, and I had to put him down in the crib for a minute just so I could breathe. I’m managing, but it’s like I’m constantly treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly unhappy—more like my mind won’t shut off. When I finally lie down, I keep replaying every little thing: Did I burp him long enough? Is that rash normal? I probably spend an hour or two staring at the ceiling three or four nights a week before I drift off.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve had moments—maybe a couple of afternoons this week—where I just felt kind of heavy and weepy for no clear reason. It’s not all day, but when it hits, everything feels gray and kind of pointless.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t actually cried. I’ve felt teary a couple of times—like yesterday when I couldn’t get the baby to latch—but the tears never quite came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt tired and overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)–style questionnaire, patient self-report, 2–3 wks postpartum.

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia: diminished capacity for pleasure/humor, “things feel gray”  
- Anxiety: near-daily “what-if” rumination, nocturnal checking, brief racing heart/chest tightness  
- Sleep disruption: initial insomnia 3–4 nights/week related to intrusive worries  
- Guilt/Self-blame: attributes infant fussiness to personal inadequacy  
- Overwhelm: constant sense of “treading water,” needs to set baby down to “breathe”  
- Low mood: intermittent afternoon sadness and weepiness, no actual crying spells

Severity indicators  
- Episodes occur “a couple of afternoons this week”  
- Functional impact: dishes pile up, naps skipped, maternal rest impaired  
- No suicidal or self-harm ideation (explicitly denied)

Screening significance  
Pattern consistent with mild-to-moderate postpartum anxiety with secondary depressive features; does not meet high-risk threshold for self-harm. Recommend formal EPDS scoring, further clinical evaluation for postpartum depression and/or anxiety disorder, psychoeducation, and support resources.

Safety: No current safety concerns identified.
